newsitem.title: CHILE: Silk ties and soccer at the Chile summit.
newsitem.headline: Silk ties and soccer at the Chile summit.

text.p: Leaders of 21 countries at the Ibero-American summit will take home the usual souvenirs of Chile, like wine, canned shellfish and dried fruit.
Fidel Castro will take home an expensive silk tie.

The Cuban president and Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar had lunch together on Sunday and shared what Spanish officials described as frank talks -- in which Castro flatly rejected Aznar's calls for political reform in Cuba.
At the end of the lunch, the two leaders swapped ties as a sign of friendship. The ever-dapper Aznar gave Castro his silk Hermes tie, the officials said.
Anyone who has made the long, grueling flight from Europe to Chile knows the feeling of mild confusion when you finally step off the plane.
Portuguese President Jorge Fernando Branco de Sampaio felt it when he arrived for the summit on Friday night. In a brief arrival statement, he sent Portugal's greetings to the "people of Cuba."
Reporters shouted to him that he was in Chile, not Cuba.
Branco de Sampaio looked confused for a moment, corrected himself and said, "Just a joke to start out."
Summit meetings on Sunday coincided with a series of World Cup soccer qualifying matches throughout South America.
Some diplomats and journalists forgot all about the summit and huddled around television screens at the Casa Piedra convention centre to watch the matches live.
The crowd watching the Colombia-Bolivia match grew so large that summit staff had to carry over extra chairs.

The menu at Saturday's night gala dinner for the summiteers at the presidential palace was classically Chilean. It included Patagonian king crab, salmon with mushrooms and scallops and a dessert made from cherimoya-fruit and orange.
Unseasonably warm weather in Santiago allowed for dining al fresco in the palace's patio.

But the hot weather caused problems at the summit, where the giant tent housing the press centre and meeting rooms often felt like a sauna. Organisers installed fans but many people spent the summit with their shirts stuck to their backs.
